outcomes.text: Explain scarcity, opportunity cost, specialisation, business purpose, and how businesses create and increase added value.
Classify businesses by primary, secondary and tertiary sectors, and distinguish private- and public-sector enterprises in a mixed economy.
Explain entrepreneurship, business plans, start-up support, business-size measurement, growth methods, reasons for remaining small, and business failure.
Compare business ownership forms, liability, risk and public corporations, then recommend a suitable organisation for a situation.
Explain changing business objectives, social-enterprise aims, stakeholder interests and conflicts, and differences between private- and public-sector objectives.
Explain workforce motivation, human needs, motivational theories, financial and non-financial methods, and justify suitable approaches in context.
Interpret organisational charts, explain management functions, delegation, leadership styles and trade unions, and justify suitable leadership choices.

topics.title: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees

subtopics.title: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees

outcomes.text: Explain recruitment, selection, training, employment types, workforce reduction, employment law, and justify hiring and redundancy decisions.
Explain communication’s importance, compare communication methods, recommend suitable methods, and identify and reduce communication barriers.
Explain marketing’s role, changing customer spending and needs, competition, niche and mass marketing, and market segmentation.
Explain market research purposes, primary and secondary methods, sampling and accuracy, and analyse results presented in charts or diagrams.
Apply product, price, place, promotion and technology concepts, including product life cycles, pricing, distribution, e-commerce and social media.
Justify marketing strategies, assess legal controls, and evaluate opportunities, problems and solutions when entering foreign markets.
Explain production, productivity, efficiency, inventories, lean production, production methods and technology’s effects, recommending suitable methods.

topics.title: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

subtopics.title: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

outcomes.text: Classify costs, explain economies and diseconomies of scale, construct and interpret break-even analysis, calculate margins of safety, and make decisions.
Explain quality’s importance and distinguish how businesses implement quality control and quality assurance.
Evaluate location and relocation factors for manufacturing and services, including country choice and legal controls, then justify a suitable location.
Explain why businesses require finance, including starting, expanding and funding additional working capital.
Identify internal and external finance sources and give examples.
Understand why businesses need finance and evaluate suitable internal and external short-term or long-term funding sources.

subtopics.title: The importance of cash and of cash-flow forecasting

outcomes.text: Explain why cash is important to a business.
Explain the meaning and importance of working capital.
Understand cash-flow forecasts and working capital, including how to prepare, interpret and manage short-term cash-flow problems.

subtopics.title: What profit is and why it is important

outcomes.text: Explain how a business generates profit.
Identify key income-statement items, including revenue, sales costs, gross profit, profit and retained profit.
Understand how profit is generated, why it matters, how it differs from cash, and how income statements support decisions.

subtopics.title: The main elements of a statement of financial position

outcomes.text: Classify assets and liabilities and provide examples of each.

subtopics.title: Interpret a simple statement of financial position and make deductions from it

outcomes.text: Interpret a simple statement of financial position to assess financing, asset ownership and inventory sales for finance.
Understand the elements of statements of financial position and interpret them to assess business financing, assets and financial decisions.
Explain the meaning and importance of profitability.
Explain the meaning and importance of liquidity.

subtopics.title: How to interpret the financial performance of a business by calculating and analysing profitability ratios and liquidity ratios

outcomes.text: Calculate and analyse gross profit margin.

subtopics.title: Why and how accounts are used

outcomes.text: Explain the information needs of different accounts users and ratio analysts.
Understand profitability and liquidity, calculate and analyse financial ratios, and use accounts to support business decisions.
Identify the main business-cycle stages, including growth, boom, recession and slump.

subtopics.title: How government control over the economy affects business activity and how businesses may respond

outcomes.text: Identify government economic objectives, such as increasing GDP.
Understand business-cycle stages, economic indicators, government policies, and how businesses respond to changing economic conditions.

subtopics.title: Environmental concerns and ethical issues as both opportunities and constraints for businesses

outcomes.text: Explain how business activity can affect the environment, including through global warming.
Understand how environmental and ethical concerns create opportunities, constraints, responsibilities, and responses for businesses.
Explain globalisation and the reasons it has developed.

subtopics.title: Reasons for the importance and growth of multinational companies (MNCs)

outcomes.text: Explain benefits of becoming multinational and its effects on stakeholders.

subtopics.title: The impact of exchange rate changes

outcomes.text: Distinguish between exchange-rate depreciation and appreciation.
